White paper

Liquid Cooling Commissioning and Site Acceptance

Interface verification and release for single-phase cold-plate systems

Equipment on site, piping installed, a coolant distribution unit (CDU) running and servers powering on are four different facts at four different stages. None of them shows that a system can carry a training run, ride through a fault, or be taken over by an operator. This paper treats these as separate questions and asks what evidence answers each one.

It sets out a method for commissioning planning, test design, evidence review and handover on liquid-cooled AI data centre projects, written for owners, designers, equipment suppliers, contractors, integrators, commissioning teams and operators.

What's inside

  • Six functional boundaries (B1–B6). From the facility water interface to the cold-plate interface. Each boundary has a named provider, receiver, test lead, witness and approver, so interface responsibilities are assigned across suppliers before procurement.
  • Four release gates (G1–G4). Before shipment, before fill, before production and before handover. Each gate is a signed decision for a defined scope against criteria approved in advance.
  • A controlled commissioning permit. For energising load emulators and actual IT equipment batch by batch. It is explicitly not a production release.
  • Four kinds of determination. Pass, Fail, Not demonstrated and Not applicable by approval. Measurement uncertainty is handled with a stated decision rule.
  • The role and the limits of simulation. Models help choose test conditions and explain deviations. They do not replace measurement, and model evidence carries its own applicability statement.
  • Appendices for project teams. An acceptance criteria register, a model and data applicability statement, dynamic test and release records, a minimum handover package, and an evidence index by interface and stage.

The paper draws on public industry work, including guidance from the Open Compute Project, ASHRAE, the Energy Efficient HPC Working Group and DMTF, and on published case studies from U.S. national laboratories. It cites 21 sources. It is a method paper, not a standard or a field work instruction. In English, 41 pages, PDF. A Chinese edition (37 pages, PDF) is also available: choose it in the form.

OCP, ASHRAE, DMTF and other names are the property of their respective owners. Their mention does not imply endorsement or affiliation.
